owner: CC gates writes to the web_server's pane machinery and the hook.
intention: CC's last 1K lines of conversation are visible in the web server's chat pane. A hook appends structured entries to a file; the web server reads the file live through the existing pane machinery.
why: CC's conversation is currently visible only in the terminal or the web interface it was launched from. The web_server's pane system already renders live device views; this is filed edge (c) applied to CC devices — rich views for interaction panes, pulled live, rendered by render.py.
how: The hook appends structured entries to a file (file append only — the hook stays trivial). The web server reads the file live through the existing pane machinery. The constraint 'file append only' keeps the hook trivial and composes cleanly with tmux (the file is the only coupling). Last 1K lines, not the whole conversation.
traces_to: Law 10 — CC's conversation is currently unmeasured at the pane surface; this makes it visible.
Telos — the system shows its own state to its operator.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) the chat pane does not update within one beat of a new hook entry; (2) the hook writes anything beyond a structured append (no read, no parse, no network); (3) more than 1K lines are held (unbounded growth).
children: none — the hook is a file append, the pane is one more reader of the existing machinery
